raw_record.question_text: A large square is divided into smaller squares. In one of the smaller squares a diagonal is also drawn, as shown. What fraction of the large square is shaded?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large square split into four equal quadrant-sized squares. From the image, identify the shaded parts: in the upper-left quadrant, two of its four equal small squares are shaded; in the upper-right quadrant, the drawn diagonal shades exactly one triangular half of that quadrant; the lower-right quadrant is fully shaded; the lower-left quadrant is unshaded. Use the text only to confirm that all pieces are squares and the extra slanted segment is a diagonal. Compute the shaded area as fractions of the large square: upper-left contribution is half of one quadrant = 1/8, upper-right contribution is half of one quadrant = 1/8, lower-right contribution is one quadrant = 1/4, and lower-left is 0. Sum 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/4 = 1/2.
